reason: Google Calendar plus a list in Apple Notes already works for me and costs nothing. I don't want to move my calendar into another app, and I definitely don't need email and contacts bundled into my planner.
objection: It's an all-in-one app pitched as a planner. I'd be paying $12 a month to replace two free tools I'm happy with, plus a bunch of extra stuff I'd never open.
would_change_my_mind: If it worked as a thin layer on top of Google Calendar, with blocks written straight into my existing calendar and no switching apps, I might try the free plan for the end-of-block done/push/drop prompt.
